metadata.result_text:
I'll help you set up a git server with automatic deployment to a web server. This requires two main components: a bare git repository with a post-receive hook, and a web server. Here's the complete setup:

## Server Setup

Run these commands on your server as the user you'll be cloning as:

```bash
# 1. Create the git repository directory
mkdir -p /git/server
cd /git/server
git init --bare

# 2. Create the web root directory
mkdir -p /var/www/html

# 3. Create the post-receive hook
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/html"
git --work-tree=$DEPLOY_DIR --git-dir=/git/server checkout -f
EOF

# 4. Make the hook executable
chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
```

## Web Server Setup

Install and start a simple HTTP server (choose one):

**Option 1: Python (simplest)**
```bash
# Run in /var/www/html directory
cd /var/www/html
python3 -m http.server 8080
```

**Option 2: Node.js**
```bash
cd /var/www/html
npx http-server -p 8080
```

**Option 3: nginx (production)**
```bash
sudo apt-get install nginx
sudo tee /etc/nginx/sites-available/default > /dev/null <<'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080;
    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;
    index index.html;
    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }
}
EOF
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

## How It Works

1. When you push to the git server, the `post-receive` hook automatically checks out the files to `/var/www/html`
2. The web server serves those files on port 8080
3. Your workflow becomes:
   ```bash
   git clone user@server:/git/server
   cd server
   echo "hello world" > hello.html
   git add hello.html
   git commit -m "add hello.html"
   git push origin master
   ```
4. After the push completes, curl will show the file:
   ```bash
   curl http://server:8080/hello.html
   # Output: hello world
   ```

## Notes

- The post-receive hook runs with the permissions of the git user, so make sure `/var/www/html` is writable by that user (adjust permissions if needed: `
